capex_override.reason: Capex tag missing for FY2023-2025 (and all post-2019 periods) because WRB reports capex as net purchases of property, furniture and equipment. $90M is 1.49x the last filed FY2019 value (inside the 0.1x-10x band) and in line with the 9M filed net-purchase figures; it is ~2.5% of FY2025 OCF, so the choice is immaterial to the verdict.
capex_override.source: Anchor: last engine-filed capex $60,457,000 in FY2019 (10-K, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, financials_history.csv); the filer's own cash-flow statements now report the same line as net purchases of property, furniture and equipment — $53,737,000 for the nine months ended 2025-09-30 and $91,670,000 for the nine months ended 2024-09-30 (10-Q consolidated statements of cash flows, investing activities) — confirming the same order of magnitude under a tag the engine does not read.

moat_against: Commodity product — fungible risk capital repriced annually via brokers; no structural pricing power or lock-in
Softening pricing cycle — H1 2026 net premiums written barely grew YoY as rate momentum moderates
Catastrophe and social-inflation tail — Q2 2026 cat losses $62.4M; casualty loss-cost inflation can hit reserves
Reserve risk — earnings lean on loss-reserve growth and prior-year development that can reverse
Leadership transition — founder/executive chairman died in 2026; the underwriting culture must survive succession
moat_for: Decentralized specialty model — autonomous operating units with local niche expertise, shared group capital/analytics
Underwriting discipline through the cycle — combined ratio 90.0% in Q2 2026, 88.1% accident-year ex-cat, vs US P&C industry near 98.5%
Proven high returns held through a cycle — operating ROE 20.5% in Q2 2026, 20.9% in H1 2026
Cycle management — leans into hard pricing, willing to pull back and protect margin instead of chasing volume
Record investment engine — net investment income $418.7M in Q2 2026 on $34.17B net invested assets, new-money yields above book yield
moat_justification: Best-in-class specialty P&C underwriting culture: decentralized operating units with local specialty expertise, combined ratios around 90% vs an industry near 98.5%, operating ROE around 20% held through the cycle, and a proven willingness to shrink premiums when pricing is inadequate — capped at moderate because the product is still fungible risk capital repriced annually, with no customer lock-in or structural pricing power, and returns remain hostage to the pricing cycle, catastrophe luck and reserve development.
name: W. R. Berkley Corporation
one_liner: Best-in-class specialty P&C insurer, moat 6/10 — engine prints Tier B (weighted IRR 16.68%, IV@15% $84.37 vs $73.80) on a float-capitalizing OCF base, so the final tier is softened to C at low confidence; it clears 15% at ~$84 on engine numbers, ~$61 (bear IV) with a margin of safety.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH insurer artifact: the OCF-based OE base capitalizes float/reserve growth (FY2025 OCF $3,582,616,000 vs net income $1,779,403,000; NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023/2024/2025), so tier-by-numbers B overstates distributable owner's earnings — and 16.68% only just clears 15% even on that flattering base, while the maintenance (net-income) definition of OE is roughly half the conservative figure. Softened one notch to C, confidence low — same treatment as HIG (A to B) and ACGL (B to C).
